work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via a UI control
Query syntax highlighting colors adjust appropriately for the selected theme
Result panels remain fully legible in both themes
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied on subsequent page loads
No regressions or UI breakage occur in other parts of the web UI
Unit tests verify theme toggle behavior and persistence

analysis.summary: Implement a toggleable dark/light theme in the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, with user preference persisted via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add light and dark theme styles compatible with the existing UI
Ensure query syntax highlighting adapts correctly to both themes
Ensure result panels remain legible under both themes
Implement a theme toggle control in the UI
Persist user theme choice across requests using local storage
Integrate theme selection logic within the Python-rendered web UI without external frameworks
Provide unit tests covering the theme toggle functionality and persistence
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via a UI control
Query syntax highlighting colors adjust appropriately for the selected theme
Result panels remain fully legible in both themes
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied on subsequent page loads
No regressions or UI breakage occur in other parts of the web UI
Unit tests verify theme toggle behavior and persistence
risks: Ensuring consistent and accessible color contrast for syntax highlighting and panels in both themes
Integrating theme toggling seamlessly without introducing UI flicker or performance issues
Persisting and correctly applying user preferences across different browsers and sessions
Testing UI changes thoroughly given no existing frameworks and a Python-rendered UI
analysis.recommended_approach: Define CSS variables or separate CSS files for dark and light themes and toggle them via JavaScript injected into the Python-rendered pages. Use local storage to save user preference and apply it on page load. Adjust syntax highlighting styles dynamically based on the active theme. Add a toggle button in the UI for users to switch themes. Write unit tests for the theme toggle logic and persistence mechanism.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme CSS styles and update styles.py to include CSS variables for light and dark themes, and adapt existing styles to use these variables

instructions: Define CSS variables for the light theme, e.g., --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --panel-bg: #ffffff, --panel-text: #000000.

Define CSS variables for the dark theme inside a .dark-theme selector, e.g., --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #569cd6, --syntax-string: #d69d85, --panel-bg: #2d2d2d, --panel-text: #f0f0f0.
Refactor existing body and container styles to use CSS variables, for example: body { background-color: var(--bg-color); color: var(--text-color); }
Update syntax highlighting styles in styles.py to use CSS variables for colors, ensuring they adapt based on the active theme.
Update result panel styles to use --panel-bg and --panel-text variables for background and text colors respectively.
Add a CSS class .theme-toggle-btn for styling the theme toggle button with consistent styling in both themes.

implementation_steps.validation: Verify that styles.py contains CSS variables for both themes, existing styles use these variables, and syntax highlighting and panels adapt colors accordingly.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme toggle button in the UI and implement JavaScript logic to toggle themes and persist user preference in localStorage

instructions: Locate the main HTML template rendering function or variable that contains the base HTML structure.
Add a theme toggle button inside the header or navigation area with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn', with initial text '🌙 Dark Mode'.
Add a <script> block just before the closing </body> tag that implements the following logic:
- On page load, read the 'theme' value from localStorage.
- If the stored theme is 'dark', add the 'dark-theme' class to the <body> element and update the button text to '☀️ Light Mode'.
- Add an event listener to the toggle button that switches the theme between light and dark by toggling the 'dark-theme' class on <body>.
- Update localStorage with the current theme on toggle.
- Update the button text accordingly to reflect the current theme.
Ensure the JavaScript is vanilla and does not rely on external libraries.
Add any necessary CSS for the toggle button in the styles section if not already included in styles.py.

implementation_steps.validation: Confirm the HTML template includes the toggle button and embedded JavaScript that correctly toggles theme, updates localStorage, and updates button text.

implementation_steps.description: Add unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence

instructions: Create tests that simulate loading the UI and verify that the default theme is light if no localStorage value is set.
Test that toggling the theme button adds/removes the 'dark-theme' class on the body element.
Test that localStorage is updated correctly when the theme is toggled.
Test that on page load, if localStorage has 'dark', the 'dark-theme' class is applied and button text is correct.
Use a headless browser or DOM simulation library to test the JavaScript behavior if possible, or test the Python template rendering logic to ensure the toggle button is present.
Ensure tests run without external dependencies and integrate with existing test framework.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover theme toggle button presence, toggling behavior, localStorage persistence, and correct application of theme classes.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables in styles.py, added a toggle button and JavaScript logic in html_template.py to persist user preference in localStorage, and created unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence.
